judged_text: updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it searches for a calendar whose externalId equals a falsy value — dead code that can never match and always yields undefined. Any reschedule/location edit on a booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (every reference produced through the new no-credentialId branch stores result.externalId = undefined) calls events.update with calendarId undefined; googleapis throws "Missing required parameter: calendarId", the error is swallowed by the catch, and the user's Google event is never updated.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), the fallback `.find(...)` searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value, which will almost always return `undefined`, leaving `selectedCalendar` undefined. Unlike `createEvent` (which does `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`), `updateEvent`’s call site in the diff does not show a fallback to `"primary"`, so this can result in `calendar.events.update` being invoked with `calendarId` undefined. Separately, `EventManager` now persists `externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId`, but in the no-credentialId branch (`createAllCalendarEvents` -> `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`), `result.externalId` will be undefined, making later updates pass a falsy `externalCalendarId` into `updateEvent` and triggering the bad fallback path.
